name: HR Operations Specialist
description: Explains employee lists, filtering by department, counting heads, and salary formatting

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do you organize employee data in Excel?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I convert the employee list into an Excel table with a header row containing ID, Name, Department, and Salary. That way I can filter by Department to view only Engineering without deleting other staff.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do you count employees and find total salary?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: To count employees with IDs, I use =COUNT(A2:A100) because COUNT handles numbers. For salary expense, I write =SUM(D2:D100). Both formulas start with =.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do you format salary numbers and visualize department headcount?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I select the salary column and choose currency format. For headcounts, I select data for departments and create a column chart with title 'Headcount by Department' and axis labels.
